newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end sharply down on U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end sharply down on U.S. rate fears.

text.p: French shares closed sharply down on Thursday in thin volume, rattled by renewed fears of U.S. interest rate tightening following data suggesting a more robust than expected American economy.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended near their late session lows, down 2.54 percent or 58.76 points at 2,256.97, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 31 points at 2,257.0.
Volume was a slim 3.85 billion francs in post-New Year holiday trade which analysts said greased the market's slide.
"People are worried about an increase in U.S. rates because of potential inflation. Also, people are expecting a correction on Wall Street," said one trader.

After initially trimming their losses following Wall Street's higher open and a market-friendly jobless claims report, the market fell again on the U.S. NAPM index which rose to 54.0, well above the forecast for 52.3.
Several traders said the market's decline could continue, noting the CAC-40 index had broken through key support at 2,258. They said it could now be poised to test support at 2,234/2,231.
"Everyone was expecting a wave of buying in January but that happened in December. Now we're seeing position-cutting with everyone expecting a correction on Wall Street," said a trader.
But not all traders were gloomy. "The fund managers are coming back from holiday on Monday. They'll start adding to their portfolios," one said.

All of the component stocks of the CAC-40 index finished lower, except for Suez which rose 0.23 percent to 221.10 francs. One trader said many of the big losers were those which had gained the most recently.

Among big losers was construction giant Bouygues, down 5.02 percent at 511 francs, pharmaceuticals firm Rhone-Poulenc, off 4.30 percent at 169.30 francs and luxury goods firm LVMH 3.66 lower at 1,396 francs.
Shares in carmakers Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen underperformed the CAC index despite a December sales report most analysts found in line with expectations or better.
Shares in Renault fell 3.59 percent to 107.50 francs, and PSA Peugeot Citroen shares dropped 4.97 percent to 555 francs.
"The sales figures weren't too bad, and certainly not for the Peugeot group," said one analyst, who said he was unaware of any fundamental reason for the sharp fall but noted thin volume.
The French carmakers' asssociation said new car sales in December rose 1.8 percent to 144,735 units from poor year-earlier levels.
